title: Review of c14's pcell-mwall-b42 metabolic claim: the fork replicates on fresh seed 5 (36 cells -> 0 within 1000 t, fed twin 35-39), and a local ablation passes too: cutting the feed on the left half kills all 20 cells there while their 16 right-half neighbours live and divide to t=100000
summary: Fresh seed 5 of the claim's world.py (fed) and world_starve.py (feed cut everywhere at t=60000), 128^2, T=100000. From near-uniform noise the fed run makes walled cells that divide (17 persistent splits, max generation 4, merge/split 0.05; fed/seed5/sheet.png) and holds 35-39 cells after t=60000. In the starved twin all 36 cells are gone within 1000 t of the cut (cells_s5.txt; fork_s5.png: wall and catalyst gone by t=61500, only fading M). Because a global cut also passes for any open reaction-diffusion spot, I added the rubric's local ablation (world_halfstarve.py, a one-line change of world_starve.py: from t=60000 the feed is cut only for x < 64): every one of the 20 left-half cells dies within 1000 t, while the 16 right-half cells, sharing the same substrate field across the boundary, persist (15-17 cells to t=100000) and keep dividing (halfstarve_s5.png). So each cell depends on its own local supply, not on a global population effect.

observations.I: fed/seed5/sheet.png: 25-39 discrete walled cells of bounded size, t=4000-100000
observations.B: fork_s5.png fed row: a closed wall (green) around each catalyst-filled (blue) cell at every time shown
observations.E: cells_s5.txt: global cut 36 -> 0 cells by t=61000 vs fed twin 35-39 to t=100000; local cut (left half) 20 -> 0 left-half cells by t=61000 while right-half cells stay 15-17 to t=100000 (halfstarve_s5.png)
observations.D: fed/seed5/lineage.png: 17 persistent splits, max generation 4 from noise-born cells, merge/split 0.053; halfstarve_s5.png t=69500 shows a right-half cell dividing after the cut

seeds_run.result: pass: fed 35-39 cells; global fork 36 -> 0 within 1000 t; half-domain fork 20 -> 0 on the cut side, 16 kept on the fed side

controls_run.E: starve/seed5 (global cut at t=60000) and halfstarve/seed5 (world_halfstarve.py, cut only for x < 64), both against the fed twin fed/seed5, identical until t=60000

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed. Death is very fast (< 1000 t against cell lifetimes of ~10^4 t), so starvation acts almost like switching the cells off; E remains by construction (links and particles need substrate and decay). After the half cut no cell colonises the starved half, so the right-half population stays near 16 rather than growing. I did not check heredity (H) or the wall's twin.
